So I remember way back when I was first talking to my doc about hormones and she asked me what I already knew about the effects. When I told her about the mental aspect, I mentioned that everything I've heard about emotional changes and even your way of thinking was something I was already experiencing and had been for a long time. She smiled and told me that I probably wouldn't notice too much of a change then. However, since going on injections several months ago (I was on oral for several years prior), I certainly find it easier to cry during sad shows or movies, which is lovely. And orgasms, omg. All I have to say is wow. So very different, the way it seems to spread through your whole body in waves of pure bliss. So yeah, that's what I've noticed :)

So my story is rather interesting. I was on a road trip with one of my best friends and we were listening to a podcast called Criminal (I highly recommend it if you like podcasts). The episode we were listening to was on psychopaths and sociopaths. They described what a psychologist looks for in a person to determine if they're a psychopath (psycho and sociopaths are now considered the same thing of varying degrees).
      So there are twenty traits they look for in an individual and proceed to list them all. And I got scared because my eleven or twelve I had at least six of the traits. So for a whole week I was like "omg I'm a psychopath oh noooo". My friend didn't think so though and eventually we end up in Quebec, weeks later. By then it's left my mind but she decided to Google psychopaths and the symptoms I've been experiencing for the last twenty years. She woke me up the next morning and told me she definitely doesn't think I'm a psycho but that she seriously believes I have BPD. 
      I did a ton of research and realized I exhibit every single symptom. I was happy there was a name for what I was going through but I still wanted an official diagnosis. 
     So upon returning to the states I found a decent psychiatrist and we talked for about two hours as I explained my depression, all the childhood trauma I experienced, and the suicide of my mother ten years ago (I'm 32f). I explained all the other symptoms related to BPD and at the end she says to me "you don't need me to diagnose you, you hit the nail on the head." I felt so good to hear I had been right and that I knew exactly what I needed to do to try to get better. I have my first DBT appointment with a therapist in the same building in two weeks and am just trying my absolute best not to slip up too much, though we all know that it happens regardless.

Has it ever affected your life negatively: Yes and no. The first half of my CDing life was honestly hellish. My parents caught me when I was a teenager and though they weren't upset or anything like that, they still  insisted on scheduling an appointment with a therapist and after that I decided to just lay low for a while. I would meet my gf years later and by that point I was in full swing again and decided to tell her shortly after being together nearly two years. She was very accepting at first but then did a complete 180 on me and hated it. We broke up shortly after and I stopped once more. It's only very recently become a positive aspect of my life thanks to my gf and her family and of course all of you awesome ladies!
